deviations.what: a CPU throughput benchmark (src/bench_cpu.py) loaded Qwen/Qwen3-4B on 96 synthetic gardening prompts BEFORE the prereg freeze
deviations.why: the grid had to be sized for a CPU-only box (no GPU; sibling agent using ~1.6 of 2 cores)
deviations.impact: no stimulus, probe item or outcome was touched; only timings were recorded (results/bench_cpu.json)

deviations.what: T1 compares the recomputed iteration-2 LENS BL1 (HARD stimuli) to 4.99/3.07, not BL1_truelogit
deviations.why: the plan's reference numbers are the lens convention (double final norm) on HARD stimuli; BL1_truelogit recomputed from the same arrays is 6.21/4.65 (HARD) and 6.65/7.46 (EASY)
deviations.impact: unit check passes under the correct convention; BL1_truelogit is still the readout used under intervention (final logits once), reported beside the lens value

deviations.what: gen_sites: judged generation beyond the frozen CPU-fallback grid (gensites)
deviations.why: slack compute after the prereg site-P grid; tests the registered prediction that F at the response sites (D', E) moves behaviour less than at P, and adds judged R_F draws 2-3 at P
deviations.impact: additional cells only; no prereg cell/outcome is altered. Decode-site R uses the OWN-coefficient random control h-(h.F)u (plan formulation) because a cross-row source trajectory diverges

deviations.what: gen_Pdraws: judged generation beyond the frozen CPU-fallback grid (genPdraws)
deviations.why: slack compute after the prereg site-P grid; tests the registered prediction that F at the response sites (D', E) moves behaviour less than at P, and adds judged R_F draws 2-3 at P
deviations.impact: additional cells only; no prereg cell/outcome is altered. Decode-site R uses the OWN-coefficient random control h-(h.F)u (plan formulation) because a cross-row source trajectory diverges

deviations.what: the plan's PRIMARY GPU design (sites P, D', E; judged generation on all 18 cells; 48+48 items; 80 new tokens; stimro, decodgen, spanD/E, gsm) runs in addition to the frozen CPU-fallback F1 cells
deviations.why: the pod restarted at ~18:23 UTC onto a box with an NVIDIA L4; the F1 prereg (17:24 UTC) was frozen on a CPU-only box
deviations.impact: the F1 cells run unchanged and are analysed as registered; every addition is frozen in prereg_gpu_addendum.json (sha256 524c15c0...) at 18:39 UTC, before any Qwen3-4B outcome was computed

deviations.what: engine hooks generalised to S trailing positions and ported to CUDA (hook hash 6e406f7f replaces the CPU session's d327a7be); all cells recomputed on the GPU
deviations.why: sites D/E need multi-position teacher-forced windows and decode-call edits
deviations.impact: hook checks a1 (no-op == hooks removed, bitwise), a2 (arm-0 rows bitwise-unaffected by co-batched active rows), b (residual along the direction < 1e-3 after the bf16 cast) and c (matched R/F displacement ratio 1 +- 1e-7) pass on smoke, instruct and saferl

deviations.what: at decode sites (D', E) the random control uses the plan's own-coefficient formula x <- x - (x.v)u; its mean displacement exceeds the treatment's (~1.4x for F, ~2x for N6 in the smoke run) because the F row loses its F component at the first band layer while the R row keeps it
deviations.why: a cross-row matched source is undefined once trajectories diverge; the exact matched design is kept at site P and in the teacher-forced span windows
deviations.impact: the D'/E control is STRONGER than the treatment in displacement: F-R is conservative for CAUSAL claims but can inflate 'decodable but inert' counts at D'/E; ratios are reported per cell

deviations.what: a second environment .venv_gpu (torch 2.9.1+cu128) is used for the GPU run; .venv (torch 2.9.1+cpu) is used for the analysis
deviations.why: the session-2 .venv had a CPU-only torch wheel
deviations.impact: none on outcomes; pyproject.toml + uv.lock record the cu128 index

deviations.what: optional 9(b): judged F_perpU arm at site P, all 6 bands (exploratory)
deviations.why: GPU slack after the primary grid
deviations.impact: additional exploratory cells only; not in any Holm family

deviations.what: T3 disambiguation control: F / N6 projected out at ALL positions (every prompt position and every decode call) per band and in all 36 layers (ALL), judged, with own-coefficient random controls
deviations.why: the site-local F arm at P changes token 1 in ~50% of rows but barely moves judged refusal; the plan's T3 requires ruling out a hook/sign/direction problem before calling site-local cells null
deviations.impact: additional exploratory cells; not in the confirmatory Holm families

genU_exploratory_FperpU.note: EXPLORATORY (plan 9b): not in any Holm family, no CAUSAL flag; tests whether F's refusal effect survives removing its component along the top-8 refusal-token unembedding rows (the N2/N3 axis)

e2x2_E_site_readout.note: d = Cohen's d(hazardous, benign) of proj_late (LATE window, tokens 40-55, unedited continuation) after an EARLY-window (tokens 5-20) edit; Delta_d(arm)=d(arm)-d(0); bootstrap resamples item_uid clusters (both prefix families of a resampled item_uid move together, same resample used for arm and for 0)

genG_global_ablation_control.note: EXPLORATORY T3 disambiguation positive control: site=ALLPOS projects F/N6 out at every prompt position and decode call within the band's layers (B1-B6) or all layers (ALL) -- inference-time ablation, not a single-site edit. Not in any Holm family, no CAUSAL determination. F_site_P_for_comparison is the matching site-P judged cell (arm F vs RF) from causal_grid_judged, for local-vs-global comparison. RFo/RN6o are own-coefficient random controls, a single draw (draw 1) each.
